correctness.rationale: A legal transfer from (u,v) to (v,w) enforces the two stationary neighbor tests precisely at v. The n transitions anchored at the labelled rungs are in bijection with fixed configurations; for a twist, extending the rungs by rail swap at i+n checks both sides of the seam, giving trace(JT^n) rather than an orbit quotient. The rung-swap commutes with T; the stationary count difference is twice the trace of the 36-dimensional odd sector. An independent exact reconstruction certified the stated antisymmetric polynomial, its Newton sums, and small direct graph counts (15,39) and (93,135). The ancillary 45-dimensional even polynomial was separately checked by summing transitions into each rail orbit, computing traces of powers through 45 and applying Newton identities modulo nine distinct primes near 10^6. Their product exceeds 10^54, above the bound on any coefficient discrepancy: each true coefficient is bounded by 10^45 from eigenvalue modulus ≤9 and the displayed polynomial has coefficient l1 norm below 10^6. The second quartic factors as (z²−φ²z+φ²)(z²−φ⁻²z+φ⁻²), yielding arguments ±π/5 and ±2π/5. The other quartic has all roots strictly inside radius 3/2 by Rouché. Using the positive exact margin at n=16 and the decreasing relative error thereafter certifies the leading-cosine sign. The exact integer recurrence covers n=3–15 with no zero and reproduces the required signs.
residual_risks: No conclusion about eventual convergence, transients or non-fixed periodic orbits; inputs and counts are labelled and use the specified open-neighbor, incumbent-retaining plurality rule.

broader_coverage.reasoning: Neither a binary specialization nor a general equilibrium framework yields the all-length ternary result. In particular the triple of distinct opinions, accepted at any incumbent in this model, has no binary counterpart.

claim_vs_prior_implication.reasoning: Labelled transfer and twisted closure are available methods. None of the compared results implies the ternary transfer polynomial or the sign and lower-order terms; those require resolving new local admissibility counts and bounding the resulting spectrum.

evidence: Apt et al. study graph coordination games; in a cubic graph with the entire common three-color palette, each color gives payoff one in the all-distinct case and otherwise the unique plurality is the unique best response, so fixed states here are exactly pure Nash equilibria.

Sánchez Muñoz–Mc Gettrick count two-choice anti-coordination equilibria on ladders, while the prism public-goods rule activates at zero or three active neighbors, neither of which has the same local predicate.
equivalent_formulations.reasoning: The PNE restatement is exact but is not an enumeration given by the general coordination-game paper. Changing best-response rules or the palette does not preserve the set of locally admissible rung transitions.

value.rationale: A single natural boundary twist produces both signs of the stationary-state difference in an exact ten-residue pattern for all lengths, with a golden-ratio spectral correction. This is a non-obvious comparison on canonical cubic graphs, useful also as a labelled pure-equilibrium enumeration; it is stronger than a small case check or the generic transfer construction. The analytic sign certificate matters because finite counts alone cannot exclude later sign deviations.
residual_risks: The result quantifies equilibria, not stability or dynamic attraction, and says nothing about other palettes or strips.
